name: Windfall
oracle_text: Each player discards their hand, then draws cards equal to the greatest number of cards a player discarded this way.
blocked_sentences: Each player discards their hand, then draws cards equal to the greatest number of cards a player discarded this way.

needs.what: A value leaf that reports, during a single resolution, the greatest number of cards any one player discarded to an earlier effect of that same resolution -- so a later `draw` in the same effect list can use it as its amount for every player. Concretely: the discard step of `for_each_player` must record a per-player count, and the value leaf must return the maximum of those counts.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `value_keys` has no discard-count leaf at all: `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn` is a turn-wide graveyard tally, not per-player and not scoped to this spell (it would also count anything else that hit a graveyard this turn, and would miss a discard replaced into exile), and `cards_in_hand` / `max_count_of` read the board at the moment the `draw` op executes -- by then every hand is empty, so both evaluate to 0. `max`/`extreme_value` can only take the maximum of leaves that already exist, and none of them expresses 'discarded this way'.

needs.what: A general way to capture a computed number early in an effect list and reuse it in a later op of the same resolution (a named/stashed amount), which is what 'X, then each player draws X' spells need.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `snapshot` is documented as reading a value off an object after its target has left the zone -- it is object-scoped last-known-information, not a per-player numeric register, so it cannot hold 'the greatest hand size among all players, measured before the discard' and hand it to a subsequent `draw`.
